catalogue: Australian house-scale mechanical heating, cooling and ventilation components

objects.name: residential mechanical-services installation
objects.definition: The fixed heating, cooling, air-distribution, mechanical-ventilation, condensate and control equipment installed to serve a house, excluding portable appliances and the separate electrical, gas and sanitary-drainage systems that connect to it.
functions: Heat, cool or ventilate selected spaces
Coordinate fixed equipment, routes, terminals, supports and controls

cad.pattern: One or more coordinated systems branching through the building
cad.placement: Plant positions, roofs, external walls, ceiling spaces, floors and occupied rooms
cad.end: Room terminals, emitters and exhaust discharge points
cad.opening: Requires coordinated penetrations, access zones and service routes
cad.load: Equipment and distribution loads transferred through dedicated supports to building structure

notes: This is a coordination assembly, not a claim that every house contains every listed system.

objects.name: refrigerated air-conditioning system
objects.definition: A fixed vapour-compression system that moves heat between indoor and outdoor air through one or more indoor units, outdoor equipment, refrigerant pipework, condensate drainage, controls and electrical connections.
functions: Heat indoor air where reverse-cycle operation is provided
Move heat through a closed refrigerant circuit

cad.pattern: Connected indoor and outdoor equipment joined by paired refrigerant and service routes
cad.placement: Indoor rooms or ceiling space and an external or plant location
cad.start: Indoor heat exchanger or conditioned-air side
cad.opening: Refrigerant, condensate, electrical and sometimes duct penetrations
cad.load: Equipment mass, vibration and pipe loads carried by dedicated supports

notes: Reverse cycle is a capability; a cooling-only system is still refrigerated air conditioning.

objects.name: single-split air-conditioning system
objects.definition: A split air-conditioning arrangement with one indoor unit connected by refrigerant pipework to one matching outdoor unit.
functions: Condition one room or connected zone
Separate indoor air treatment from outdoor compressor and heat exchange
Provide a maintained refrigerant connection between two units

cad.pattern: One indoor unit, one outdoor unit and one paired service route
cad.placement: Indoor room or ceiling zone connected to an outdoor equipment position
cad.opening: Usually one coordinated wall, ceiling or floor penetration route
cad.load: Each unit independently supported; pipework clipped along route

objects.name: multi-split air-conditioning system
objects.definition: A split air-conditioning arrangement in which two or more individually controlled indoor units connect through refrigerant pipework to one outdoor unit.
functions: Branch refrigerant distribution to individually controlled indoor units

cad.pattern: One outdoor unit feeding a branching pipe network to two or more indoor units
cad.placement: Outdoor plant location with indoor units distributed through rooms
cad.opening: Multiple service penetrations or shared trunk route with branches
cad.load: Units independently supported and pipes clipped along each branch

notes: The permitted indoor-unit combinations and branch hardware are selected-product data.

objects.name: ducted reverse-cycle air-conditioning system
objects.definition: A split heat-pump system with a concealed indoor fan-coil unit connected to supply and return ductwork that heats or cools multiple spaces.
functions: Provide central heating and refrigerated cooling
Serve multiple outlets and optional zones

ncc_references.relationship: Heating and cooling ductwork and fittings require insulation and air sealing subject to location and system type.

cad.pattern: Central indoor fan coil with branching supply network and one or more return paths
cad.placement: Indoor unit commonly in ceiling or plant space; ducts through service zones
cad.opening: Ceiling and wall outlets plus service, return and access openings
cad.load: Indoor and outdoor units and ductwork independently supported

objects.name: mechanical air-distribution system
objects.definition: The connected ducts, fittings, plenums, dampers, supports, insulation, seals, supply outlets and return inlets that move air between mechanical equipment and rooms.
functions: Carry supply, return, outdoor or exhaust air
Divide and balance airflow between branches
Deliver or collect air at room terminals

ncc_references.relationship: Heating and cooling ductwork and fittings are subject to insulation and sealing provisions.

cad.pattern: Branching routed network from equipment plenums to terminal points
cad.placement: Roof, ceiling, wall, floor, bulkhead and plant spaces
cad.start: Equipment air connection or outdoor terminal
cad.end: Room grille, diffuser or external terminal
cad.opening: Passes through construction and terminates in framed or cut openings
cad.load: Duct and fitting weight transferred through hangers, straps, brackets or bearing supports

notes: Supply, return, outdoor-air and exhaust-air paths remain separately identifiable even when they share a service zone.

objects.name: split-system refrigerant pipework assembly
objects.definition: The paired refrigerant pipes, insulation, joints, branch fittings, service valves, clips and protective covering that connect split-system indoor and outdoor equipment.
functions: Protect pipes from heat gain, condensation, weather and physical damage

cad.pattern: Two parallel insulated pipe runs with joints and branches at documented points
cad.placement: Between indoor and outdoor equipment through wall, ceiling, floor or surface capping
cad.opening: Passes through sleeved and sealed building penetrations
cad.load: Pipe weight and thermal movement carried by clips and equipment connections

notes: Refrigerant charge and safety classification are metadata, not a drawable solid volume by default.

objects.name: air-conditioning condensate drainage assembly
objects.definition: The drain pan outlet, graded drain pipe, fittings, trap where selected, pump where required, insulation, supports and lawful discharge connection that remove water condensed at cooling equipment.
functions: Drain or pump condensate to an approved point
Prevent leakage and unwanted surface condensation along the route

cad.pattern: One or more graded branches from equipment drain pans to discharge
cad.placement: Below indoor cooling or ventilation equipment through ceiling, wall or exterior routes
cad.end: Approved visible or connected discharge point
cad.opening: Requires pipe penetrations and accessible pump or trap positions
cad.load: Pipe and pump supported independently of flexible drain connections

notes: The permitted discharge point is jurisdiction- and project-specific and must not be guessed by a drawing tool.

objects.name: mechanical-equipment support assembly
objects.definition: The brackets, bases, frames, feet, anchors and vibration-control components that hold fixed mechanical equipment at its documented position.
functions: Carry equipment dead and operating loads
Maintain clearance, drainage and service access

cad.pattern: One support set beneath or behind each supported equipment unit
cad.placement: Ground, slab, wall, roof, platform or ceiling structure
cad.opening: Maintains service, airflow and drainage clearances
cad.load: Transfers equipment mass, operating vibration and environmental actions to structure

notes: Structural adequacy and wind restraint require project-specific design rather than a generic bracket shape.

objects.name: ducted air-conditioning zone-control system
objects.definition: A coordinated set of controller, room or zone sensors, interface modules, actuators and motorised duct dampers that varies airflow to selected groups of rooms.
functions: Open, close or modulate zone air paths
Coordinate zone demand with the air-conditioning unit

cad.pattern: One central controller linked to distributed sensors and branch dampers
cad.placement: Controller in occupied area; sensors in zones; actuators at accessible duct branches
cad.end: Motorised damper actuators and equipment interface
cad.opening: Controllers and sensors occupy wall positions; dampers occupy duct sections
cad.load: Devices supported by walls, ducts or equipment enclosures

notes: A closed-zone airflow or pressure strategy is design metadata and cannot be inferred from damper count alone.

objects.name: ducted evaporative-cooling system
objects.definition: A fixed cooling system that draws outdoor air through wetted evaporative media and distributes the cooled air through ducts to rooms, with water supply, drainage, controls and an air-relief strategy.
functions: Cool incoming outdoor air by water evaporation
Manage water circulation, drain-off and room air relief

ncc_references.relationship: Evaporative cooling ductwork is included in the heating-only or cooling-only insulation path.

cad.pattern: One roof or platform cooler feeding a branching supply-only duct network
cad.placement: Commonly roof-mounted with ducts in roof space and outlets through ceilings
cad.end: Supply outlets and deliberate building air-relief openings
cad.opening: Roof dropper and room outlet openings
cad.load: Operating weight and wind transferred through roof stand, dropper or platform

notes: Evaporative cooling adds outdoor air; it does not recirculate room air in the same way as a refrigerated ducted system.

objects.name: whole-house heat-recovery ventilation system
objects.definition: A balanced mechanical-ventilation arrangement that extracts stale indoor air and supplies filtered outdoor air through separate ducts while transferring heat between the two air streams in a heat-exchanger core.
functions: Extract stale or moist indoor air
Recover heat between separated air streams

cad.pattern: One central unit with four distinguishable duct paths and distributed terminals
cad.placement: Ceiling, plant cupboard or service space with accessible filters and drain
cad.start: Outdoor intake and indoor extract terminals
cad.end: Indoor supply and outdoor exhaust terminals
cad.opening: Requires external intake and discharge penetrations plus room terminals
cad.load: Unit and ducts independently suspended or supported

notes: HRV and ERV are not automatic synonyms: moisture transfer depends on the core and selected product.

objects.name: residential hydronic heating system
objects.definition: A closed or controlled water-based heating system with a heat source, circulation equipment, flow and return piping, safety and fill components, controls and room or floor emitters.
functions: Heat water or another permitted heat-transfer liquid
Return cooler liquid to the heat source

ncc_references.relationship: Central-heating water-pipe insulation material and protection.
Central-heating water-pipe insulation according to location and climate zone.

cad.pattern: Closed flow and return network from heat source to one or more emitter branches
cad.placement: Plant area, wall and floor service routes, slab or floor build-up and occupied rooms
cad.start: Hydronic heat source and supply header
cad.opening: Pipe penetrations, manifold cabinets and emitter fixing zones
cad.load: Equipment and water mass carried by bases, brackets and pipe supports

notes: Heating water is a separate closed-loop service from potable domestic hot water unless a documented heat exchanger connects the systems.

objects.name: hydronic underfloor-heating assembly
objects.definition: A hydronic emitter made from one or more heating-pipe circuits fixed within or below a floor and connected to a distribution manifold, controls and the hydronic flow and return system.
functions: Distribute low-temperature radiant heat across a floor
Divide the floor into controllable pipe circuits
Transfer heat through the floor finish into the room

cad.pattern: Repeated serpentine or spiral pipe loops returning to one manifold
cad.placement: Within slab, screed, suspended-floor panel or below-floor system
cad.opening: Manifold cabinet and floor penetrations at loop tails
cad.load: Pipe is held by floor system; manifold carried by wall cabinet or bracket

notes: Loop spacing, length and floor construction are design inputs and must not be hard-coded as universal values.

objects.name: hydronic radiator assembly
objects.definition: A wall or floor-mounted water-heating emitter with radiator body, brackets, flow and return connections, control and balancing valves and an air vent.
functions: Transfer heat from circulating water to a room
Permit balancing, isolation and air release

cad.pattern: One radiator body with paired valves and wall supports at each scheduled room location
cad.placement: On wall or floor near selected room heat-loss locations
cad.start: Hydronic flow connection and control valve
cad.opening: Pipe tails pass through wall or floor; vent remains accessible
cad.load: Filled radiator mass transferred through rated brackets or feet

objects.name: split-system outdoor unit
objects.definition: The outdoor part of a split air-conditioning or heat-pump system, containing the compressor, outdoor heat exchanger, fan, valves, controls and casing connected to indoor equipment by refrigerant pipework.
functions: Provide outdoor-side valves and service access

cad.pattern: One outdoor unit per single-split system or documented shared unit
cad.placement: Outdoor ground, wall, roof, balcony or plant position with clear airflow and service access
cad.end: Fan discharge and refrigerant service valves
cad.opening: Keep grille, fan and service panels unobstructed
cad.load: Operating mass and vibration carried through feet or brackets

notes: Condenser unit is common trade language, but the outdoor coil acts as an evaporator during reverse-cycle heating.

objects.name: multi-split outdoor unit
objects.definition: An outdoor refrigerating unit designed to connect to two or more compatible, individually controlled indoor units through a branching refrigerant network.
functions: Provide multiple or branched refrigerant connections
not_synonyms: one outdoor unit serving one indoor unit

cad.pattern: One shared outdoor unit connected to several indoor branches
cad.placement: Outdoor position with airflow, pipe-route and service access
cad.opening: Keep grille, fan and service panels unobstructed
cad.load: Operating mass and vibration carried through feet or brackets

objects.name: split-system indoor unit
objects.definition: The indoor part of a split air-conditioning system, containing an indoor heat exchanger, fan, filter, condensate pan, air openings, casing and controls or control interfaces.
functions: Draw in room or return air
Return conditioned air and collect cooling condensate

cad.pattern: One or more indoor units at scheduled room or duct positions
cad.placement: Wall, floor, ceiling, bulkhead or ceiling space according to unit form
cad.opening: Air openings, service panels, pipe and drain routes remain accessible
cad.load: Unit mass carried by wall plate, rods, frame or floor supports

notes: Fan coil is acceptable in context but can also describe hydronic equipment, so the refrigerant or water connection must remain explicit.

objects.name: wall-mounted split-system indoor unit
objects.definition: A high-wall indoor air-conditioning unit with a rear mounting plate, upper or front return-air intake, filter and directed supply-air outlet.
functions: Condition one room or open zone
Mount compact equipment high on a wall
Direct supply air through adjustable vanes

cad.pattern: One elongated unit high on each scheduled wall
cad.placement: High on internal wall with unobstructed return and supply air
cad.start: Rear mounting plate and return-air intake
cad.opening: Wall service penetration commonly behind or beside unit
cad.load: Unit mass transferred through mounting plate to wall framing or masonry

objects.name: floor-console split-system indoor unit
objects.definition: A low-level indoor air-conditioning unit fixed at or near floor level, with room-air intake and one or more conditioned-air discharge paths.
functions: Condition a room from a low wall position
Provide accessible low-level intake and discharge
Connect to concealed refrigerant and drain services

cad.pattern: One compact upright unit at low wall level
cad.placement: Against internal wall at floor level
cad.opening: Rear or side pipe and drain penetration
cad.load: Unit bears on floor or wall brackets and is restrained to wall

objects.name: ceiling-cassette air-conditioning indoor unit
objects.definition: A recessed ceiling indoor unit with its equipment body above the ceiling and a visible intake-and-discharge fascia at ceiling level.
functions: Condition a room from the ceiling
Provide removable filter and service access through or near the fascia

cad.pattern: One recessed square or rectangular unit centred in a ceiling zone
cad.placement: Suspended above ceiling with fascia flush to ceiling face
cad.opening: Requires ceiling cut-out and service access
cad.load: Suspended from structure independently of ceiling lining

objects.name: bulkhead air-conditioning indoor unit
objects.definition: A compact concealed indoor fan-coil unit installed within a ceiling bulkhead and connected to short supply and return openings or ducts.
functions: Hide indoor equipment within a bulkhead
Condition an adjacent room or zone
Connect compact equipment to architectural grilles

cad.pattern: One slim concealed unit per local bulkhead zone
cad.placement: Within framed bulkhead above accessible ceiling or grille
cad.start: Return grille or short return duct
cad.end: Supply grille or short supply duct
cad.opening: Requires bulkhead grilles and service-access opening
cad.load: Suspended from structure or supported on dedicated frame

objects.name: ducted split-system indoor fan-coil unit
objects.definition: A concealed split-system indoor unit designed for connection to supply and return ductwork, containing a refrigerant coil, blower, filter interface and condensate pan.
functions: Provide fan pressure for a duct network
Collect condensate and connect to refrigerant services

cad.pattern: One concealed central unit connected to supply and return plenums
cad.placement: Ceiling, roof or plant space with service and filter access
cad.opening: Duct connections, access panel, refrigerant and drain routes
cad.load: Suspended by rods or supported on dedicated platform independently of ducts

objects.name: packaged window-or-wall air conditioner
objects.definition: A self-contained room air conditioner installed through a window or wall opening, with indoor and outdoor air sides contained within one casing.
functions: Reject or collect heat at the outdoor side
Combine the refrigerating circuit within one through-opening unit

cad.pattern: One rectangular unit spanning an envelope opening
cad.placement: Through external wall or window opening
cad.opening: Occupies framed and weather-sealed envelope opening
cad.load: Unit mass supported by wall, window frame and dedicated bracket as required

notes: Portable air conditioners with flexible exhaust hoses are outside the fixed-building scope unless deliberately scheduled.

objects.name: multi-split refrigerant branch box
objects.definition: A proprietary enclosed fitting assembly that divides or controls refrigerant flow between one multi-split outdoor unit and several indoor-unit branches.
functions: Distribute refrigerant to multiple indoor units
Consolidate service connections at an accessible point

cad.pattern: One enclosed branch device at a documented refrigerant network node
cad.placement: Accessible ceiling or service space between outdoor and indoor branches
cad.opening: Requires service clearance and pipe entries
cad.load: Device independently bracketed or suspended

notes: Only generate a branch box where the selected product architecture requires one.

objects.name: air-conditioning refrigerant compressor
objects.definition: A motor-driven component within refrigerating equipment that raises refrigerant pressure and circulates refrigerant through the vapour-compression circuit.
functions: Provide the principal mechanical input to the refrigeration cycle

cad.pattern: One or more sealed compressor bodies inside outdoor equipment
cad.placement: Within outdoor-unit casing on vibration mounts
cad.opening: Internal service clearance within casing
cad.load: Mass and vibration transferred through internal mounts to chassis

notes: Normally represented only at detailed equipment level, not in early architectural models.

objects.name: air-conditioning outdoor heat-exchanger coil
objects.definition: A finned refrigerant coil inside an outdoor unit that exchanges heat between the refrigerant circuit and outdoor air.
functions: Transfer heat between refrigerant and outdoor air
Act as condenser in cooling mode
Act as evaporator in reverse-cycle heating mode

cad.pattern: One wraparound, flat or multiple coil panels behind outdoor grilles
cad.placement: Within outdoor-unit casing around fan air path
cad.opening: Air passes through fin field
cad.load: Coil supported by outdoor-unit chassis

notes: Condenser coil is mode-dependent language in a reverse-cycle system.

objects.name: air-conditioning indoor heat-exchanger coil
objects.definition: A finned refrigerant coil inside an indoor unit that exchanges heat between the refrigerant circuit and room or return air.
functions: Cool and dehumidify air in cooling mode
Heat air in reverse-cycle heating mode
Transfer condensate to the drain pan when cooling

cad.pattern: One finned coil field inside each indoor unit
cad.placement: Downstream of filter and upstream of supply fan or outlet according to unit design
cad.opening: Air passes through fin field
cad.load: Coil supported by indoor-unit chassis

notes: Evaporator coil is mode-dependent language in a reverse-cycle system.

objects.name: air-conditioning indoor blower fan
objects.definition: A motor-driven fan within an indoor unit that draws air through the filter and heat exchanger and discharges conditioned air to the room or ductwork.
functions: Move return air through the indoor unit

cad.pattern: One or more fan wheels within indoor casing
cad.placement: Along the indoor unit air path
cad.opening: Fan inlet and discharge remain unobstructed
cad.load: Motor and fan supported by internal chassis and vibration mounts

objects.name: air-conditioning outdoor propeller fan
objects.definition: A motor-driven axial fan within an outdoor unit that moves outdoor air through the heat-exchanger coil and discharges it clear of the unit.
functions: Move air through the outdoor coil

cad.pattern: One or more axial fans behind an outdoor grille
cad.placement: Within outdoor-unit discharge face
cad.opening: Fan guard and discharge clearance remain unobstructed
cad.load: Motor and guard supported by equipment chassis

objects.name: air-conditioner return-air filter
objects.definition: A removable porous element at an indoor-unit or return-air intake that captures dust and debris before air passes through the coil and fan.
functions: Provide a cleanable or replaceable maintenance element

cad.pattern: One or more removable panels across return-air path
cad.placement: At indoor-unit intake or separate return-air filter grille or box
cad.opening: Removal path must remain accessible
cad.load: Filter frame seats in guides or grille frame

notes: Filter grade and pressure drop are selected-product data.

objects.name: indoor-unit condensate tray
objects.definition: A shaped pan beneath a cooling coil that collects condensed water and directs it to one or more drain outlets.
functions: Direct water to the drain connection
Contain incidental water within the unit

cad.pattern: One shaped pan under each condensing coil section
cad.placement: Inside indoor unit below coil
cad.opening: Drain port connects to external drain assembly
cad.load: Pan supported by equipment chassis and carries temporary water load

objects.name: air-conditioner equipment casing
objects.definition: The outer cabinet panels, grilles and fixed chassis surfaces enclosing an indoor or outdoor air-conditioning unit while preserving its air and service openings.
functions: Support removable panels, guards and labels

cad.pattern: Panelled enclosure surrounding each equipment chassis
cad.placement: Outer boundary of indoor or outdoor unit
cad.opening: Preserves air grilles, pipe entries and service-panel openings
cad.load: Panels supported by equipment chassis; not a building load-bearing enclosure

objects.name: mechanical-equipment access panel
objects.definition: A removable or hinged panel in a mechanical unit or adjacent building lining that provides access to filters, controls, drains, valves or other serviceable components.
functions: Close the equipment or lining opening during operation
Retain fasteners, seals and identification at an access point

cad.pattern: One panel aligned with each selected maintained component
cad.placement: On equipment casing, ceiling, wall, bulkhead or duct
cad.opening: Panel opens into a usable maintenance path
cad.load: Panel self-weight carried by frame, hinges or fasteners

notes: The access panel is physical; the working space in front of it is an analysis or clearance field.

objects.name: refrigerant expansion device
objects.definition: A metering component that reduces refrigerant pressure and controls flow into an evaporating heat exchanger.
functions: Respond to system load through fixed or controlled operation

cad.pattern: One or more small inline metering devices within refrigerant circuit
cad.placement: Inside indoor or outdoor equipment according to product design
cad.opening: Inline refrigerant passage
cad.load: Supported by pipework and equipment chassis

notes: The exact location varies by equipment architecture.

objects.name: heat-pump refrigerant reversing valve
objects.definition: A multi-port valve in a reverse-cycle refrigerant circuit that changes the direction of refrigerant flow so the indoor and outdoor coils exchange heating and cooling roles.
functions: Switch between heating and cooling circuit paths
Connect compressor suction and discharge to the selected coils

cad.pattern: One multi-port valve close to compressor pipework
cad.placement: Within reverse-cycle outdoor unit
cad.opening: Four connected refrigerant passages
cad.load: Supported by pipework and chassis restraints

notes: Cooling-only equipment does not require this component.

objects.name: refrigerant service valve
objects.definition: A valve at refrigerating equipment or pipework that provides isolation, charging, evacuation, pressure testing or service connection functions for the refrigerant circuit.
functions: Isolate part of the refrigerant circuit
Connect installed pipework to factory equipment

cad.pattern: One valve on each documented refrigerant line at equipment or service point
cad.placement: Commonly behind outdoor-unit service cover
cad.opening: Service port and stem require tool access
cad.load: Supported by equipment chassis and connected pipe

notes: Only licensed personnel may perform regulated refrigerant work; the licence itself is not a physical object.

objects.name: air-conditioner control board
objects.definition: An electronic printed-circuit assembly inside air-conditioning equipment that receives sensors and commands and controls motors, valves, compressor operation and communications.
functions: Drive or communicate with internal components

cad.pattern: One or more boards inside protected electrical compartments
cad.placement: Within indoor or outdoor unit control enclosure
cad.opening: Accessible only after service cover removal
cad.load: Board supported by standoffs inside equipment enclosure

notes: Normally represented as equipment metadata unless a detailed service model is needed.

objects.name: HVAC wall controller
objects.definition: A fixed wall-mounted user interface that commands heating, cooling or ventilation equipment and may contain a room-temperature sensor and schedule functions.
materials: display and buttons or touch surface

cad.pattern: One or more controllers at selected occupied-room positions
cad.placement: Internal wall away from misleading heat, cold and airflow sources
cad.end: Control cable or wireless equipment link
cad.opening: May use wall box or cable penetration
cad.load: Light fixture load carried by wall fixing

notes: Thermostat and controller may be combined, but their sensing and command roles should remain explicit attributes.

objects.name: air-conditioner handheld remote controller
objects.definition: A portable user-control handset supplied with compatible air-conditioning equipment, often stored in a fixed wall cradle but not hard-wired to the building.
functions: Send operating commands to an indoor unit

cad.pattern: One handset and optional wall cradle per controlled indoor unit
cad.placement: Portable within room; cradle fixed to wall where provided
cad.opening: No building opening except cradle fasteners
cad.load: Handset removable; cradle lightly fixed to wall

notes: Included because a wall cradle and scheduled handset location can be useful, but it is not a fixed building service in the same sense as wired controls.

objects.name: refrigerant gas pipe
objects.definition: The larger-diameter copper tube in a typical split-system pipe pair that carries low-pressure suction gas or, according to operating mode and circuit design, hot refrigerant gas.
functions: Carry refrigerant vapour between indoor and outdoor equipment
Complete one side of the sealed refrigerant circuit
Receive continuous vapour-control insulation where required

cad.pattern: One continuous routed tube with documented joints and branches
cad.placement: Along the indoor-to-outdoor service route
cad.opening: Passes through sleeves and protective capping where selected
cad.load: Pipe and insulation weight carried by clips without stressing equipment connections

notes: Gas pipe is refrigerant trade terminology and must not be confused with a fuel-gas service.

objects.name: refrigerant liquid pipe
objects.definition: The smaller-diameter copper tube in a typical split-system pipe pair that carries predominantly liquid refrigerant between indoor and outdoor equipment according to circuit mode and design.
functions: Carry refrigerant on the liquid side of the circuit
Connect equipment and branch fittings without leakage
materials: insulation where required by product and circuit

cad.pattern: One continuous tube routed beside the gas pipe
cad.placement: Along the indoor-to-outdoor service route
cad.opening: Passes through sleeves and protective capping where selected
cad.load: Pipe weight carried by clips without stressing equipment connections

notes: The physical state can vary locally in a working system; the name identifies the designed circuit side.

objects.name: refrigerant-pipe insulation
objects.definition: A continuous closed-cell thermal-insulation sleeve or wrap around refrigerant pipework that limits heat transfer and surface condensation and may require weather protection outdoors.
functions: Protect the refrigerant pipe from contact and minor abrasion

cad.pattern: Concentric sleeve continuously following each selected refrigerant pipe
cad.placement: Around refrigerant tubes including fittings where required
cad.opening: Joints close around pipe and fittings
cad.load: Self-weight carried by pipe; supports avoid crushing insulation

notes: Insulation selection is product- and climate-dependent; appearance alone does not establish thermal performance.

objects.name: air-conditioning service capping
objects.definition: A surface-mounted protective trunking system that encloses refrigerant pipes, condensate drain and associated cable along an exposed wall route.
functions: Form bends, offsets, entries and terminations around a combined service route

cad.pattern: Continuous rectangular or shaped surface channel with discrete fittings
cad.placement: On external or internal wall along exposed service route
cad.start: Indoor-unit wall entry or first exposed service point
cad.opening: Contains pipes, drain and cable with removable lid
cad.load: Channel and services fixed to wall substrate at selected centres

notes: The drain must retain any required fall inside the capping; the visible channel should not force a level route.

objects.name: refrigerant flare joint
objects.definition: A demountable refrigerant-pipe connection formed by a flared copper tube end compressed against a compatible fitting by a flare nut.
functions: Join copper refrigerant tube to equipment or a fitting

cad.pattern: One discrete coupling at each documented flared connection
cad.placement: At equipment valves or approved inline fittings
cad.opening: Internal refrigerant passage remains continuous
cad.load: Joint carries pipe connection forces but pipe is separately supported

notes: Connection preparation, torque and leak testing are licensed-work evidence, not geometry-derived compliance.

objects.name: brazed refrigerant-pipe joint
objects.definition: A permanent capillary or socket joint between compatible refrigerant tubes or fittings made with an approved brazing process and filler metal.

cad.pattern: Discrete socket or butt connection along pipe route
cad.placement: At approved tube extensions, equipment tails and branch fittings
cad.opening: Maintains continuous internal bore
cad.load: Pipe is separately supported on both sides of joint

notes: Brazing procedure and test evidence must remain linked records.

objects.name: refrigerant branch joint
objects.definition: A purpose-designed refrigerant fitting that divides or combines a main refrigerant line into compatible branch lines for multi-unit systems.
functions: Connect the main pipe to multiple downstream pipes

cad.pattern: One Y or header fitting at each documented refrigerant branch
cad.placement: Accessible pipe route between outdoor and indoor units
cad.opening: Internal passages divide without obstruction
cad.load: Fitting and adjacent pipes separately supported

notes: Orientation and branch lengths can be product-specific and must not be guessed.

objects.name: mechanical-service wall sleeve
objects.definition: A rigid tube or formed liner through a wall, floor or ceiling opening that protects mechanical pipes, drains or cables and defines a sealable penetration path.
functions: Protect services at the building opening
Separate services from sharp or incompatible construction
Provide a defined annular space for weather, air, acoustic or fire sealing

cad.pattern: One sleeve through each selected construction penetration
cad.placement: Through wall, floor, roof or ceiling boundary
cad.opening: Lines and protects the service opening
cad.load: Sleeve carried by host or fixed independently; services separately supported

notes: A sleeve alone does not complete weatherproofing, air sealing, acoustic sealing or fire stopping.

objects.name: mechanical-pipe escutcheon
objects.definition: A split or one-piece trim plate fitted around mechanical pipework where it passes through a visible wall, floor or ceiling surface.
functions: Cover the visible edge of a service penetration
Provide a neat finish around pipe or capping
Allow later removal where a split form is used

cad.pattern: One trim ring at each visible pipe penetration face
cad.placement: Around pipe or service bundle at finished surface
cad.opening: Central opening closely surrounds service
cad.load: Light trim fixed to surface or clipped around pipe

notes: An escutcheon is visual trim and must not be treated as the underlying weather, air or fire seal.

objects.name: mechanical-service penetration seal
objects.definition: A selected sealant, gasket, flashing or tested sealing system closing the gap between mechanical services, sleeves and the penetrated construction.
functions: Close the annular gap around services
Maintain any documented acoustic or fire performance when a suitable tested system is selected
materials: collar or wrap in tested systems

cad.pattern: Continuous seal around each selected service or sleeve perimeter
cad.placement: At one or both faces of penetrated construction according to system
cad.opening: Closes annular gap without obstructing service bore
cad.load: Accommodates limited movement; not a structural support

notes: Fire and acoustic performance require a documented tested system, not a generic bead of sealant.

objects.name: refrigerant-pipe support clip
objects.definition: A clip, clamp or saddle that fixes refrigerant pipework and its insulation or protective insert to a wall, frame, channel or other support.

cad.pattern: Repeated clips along routed pipework and at fittings as designed
cad.placement: Fixed to wall, framing, channel or independent support
cad.opening: Clip surrounds or cradles pipe without crushing insulation
cad.load: Transfers pipe weight and restraint forces to substrate

objects.name: air-conditioning condensate drain pipe
objects.definition: A graded pipe carrying condensate from an air-conditioning or ventilation unit drain outlet toward an approved discharge point or pump chamber.
functions: Connect equipment drain outlets to discharge
materials: PVC or other approved polymer pipe

cad.pattern: Continuous graded route with discrete fittings and supports
cad.placement: Below equipment through ceiling, wall or external service path
cad.start: Equipment drain outlet or pump discharge
cad.opening: Passes through sleeves and remains accessible for cleaning where required
cad.load: Water-filled pipe weight carried by clips; equipment connector unstressed

notes: A drawing tool must preserve fall and a documented destination; an apparently connected pipe may still be non-functional.

objects.name: condensate drain-pipe fitting
objects.definition: A bend, coupling, tee, reducer, adaptor or inspection fitting used to join and route air-conditioning condensate pipework.
functions: Connect equipment outlets, traps, pumps or terminations

cad.pattern: Discrete fitting at every connection, direction or size change
cad.placement: Along condensate pipe route
cad.opening: Maintains continuous drainage bore and fall
cad.load: Supported with adjacent pipe or separately where heavy

objects.name: air-conditioning condensate drain trap
objects.definition: A shaped condensate-drain fitting that maintains a water seal or pressure break where required by the equipment pressure and drainage arrangement.
functions: Permit condensate drainage against equipment air pressure
Limit air being drawn or blown through the drain
Provide a cleanable low point where designed
materials: PVC or transparent polymer pipe and fittings

cad.pattern: One U-shaped or proprietary trap near selected equipment outlet
cad.placement: Below drain pan with service and cleaning access
cad.opening: Maintains designed liquid-seal geometry
cad.load: Trap and retained water independently clipped or bracketed

notes: A trap is not universal; it is generated only when required by the equipment and drainage design.

objects.name: air-conditioning condensate pump
objects.definition: A small automatic pump and reservoir or inline pumping unit that lifts condensate where continuous gravity drainage cannot be achieved.
functions: Lift water to a higher drain route
Switch automatically with water level and provide an alarm contact where fitted

cad.pattern: One pump at each equipment location lacking gravity fall
cad.placement: Inside unit, adjacent trunking, ceiling space or accessible service position
cad.opening: Reservoir and filter require cleaning access
cad.load: Pump fixed to unit, wall or independent bracket with vibration control

notes: Pump lift, noise and alarm strategy are selected-product and project inputs.

objects.name: condensate high-level float switch
objects.definition: A water-level sensing switch in a condensate pan, reservoir or drain line that stops equipment or raises an alarm when drainage is blocked or water rises abnormally.
functions: Interrupt cooling or signal an alarm

cad.pattern: One switch at selected pan, trap or pump reservoir
cad.placement: At a high-level or overflow sensing point
cad.opening: Requires test and replacement access
cad.load: Light device supported by pan, pipe or reservoir

notes: A switch reduces risk but does not replace a correctly designed drain path.

objects.name: condensate-pipe insulation
objects.definition: A closed-cell sleeve around condensate drainage pipework used where the pipe surface may become cold enough to form unwanted external condensation.
functions: Protect the drain pipe along sensitive routes

cad.pattern: Concentric sleeve following selected condensate pipe sections
cad.placement: Around cold drain pipe in ceiling, wall or humid service zones
cad.opening: Joints close around pipe and fittings
cad.load: Self-weight carried by pipe without crushed support points

notes: Insulation need depends on water temperature, route and ambient moisture conditions.

objects.name: condensate drain terminal fitting
objects.definition: The visible adaptor, elbow, nozzle or other end fitting where an air-conditioning condensate drain discharges to its documented destination.
functions: Direct discharge without wetting vulnerable construction
Keep the outlet visible or connected as designed

cad.pattern: One terminal at the end of each independent drain route
cad.placement: At approved exterior, trapped or connected discharge point
cad.opening: Outlet remains unobstructed and inspectable where required
cad.load: Terminal and pipe clipped to substrate

notes: The catalogue does not nominate one universal discharge location.

objects.name: air-conditioner outdoor-unit wall bracket
objects.definition: A pair or frame of projecting metal brackets anchored to a wall to support a split-system outdoor unit above ground.
functions: Hold the unit clear of ground or roof
Provide fixing points for feet and vibration pads

cad.pattern: Two arms or one frame beneath outdoor-unit feet
cad.placement: Anchored to external wall at designed height
cad.opening: Maintains air, service and drainage clearances
cad.load: Transfers unit weight, vibration and environmental actions into wall structure

notes: Bracket capacity and anchors must suit the actual unit, wall and exposure.

objects.name: air-conditioner outdoor-unit ground base
objects.definition: A level concrete slab, precast pad or proprietary ground base supporting an outdoor mechanical unit above stable, drained ground.
functions: Keep equipment level and clear of soil
Provide a durable anchoring and drainage surface

cad.pattern: One base beneath each ground-mounted unit or documented group
cad.placement: On prepared drained ground beside building
cad.opening: Clear perimeter permits drainage and service access
cad.load: Transfers equipment and environmental loads into ground

notes: Ground movement, frost, flooding and termite inspection requirements remain project inputs.

objects.name: mechanical-equipment mounting foot
objects.definition: A discrete foot, rail or proprietary mounting block between mechanical equipment and its slab, platform, roof or bracket support.

cad.pattern: Repeated feet or two continuous rails below equipment base
cad.placement: Between equipment feet and slab, platform or frame
cad.opening: Maintains under-unit clearance
cad.load: Carries concentrated equipment loads into support

objects.name: mechanical anti-vibration mount
objects.definition: An elastomeric pad, bush, spring or proprietary isolator placed between mechanical equipment and its support to reduce vibration transmission.
functions: Carry equipment load within rated deflection

cad.pattern: One isolator at each documented equipment support point
cad.placement: Between unit feet or frame and supporting structure
cad.opening: Allows designed deflection without short-circuiting
cad.load: Carries allocated equipment load while isolating vibration

notes: Selection requires equipment weight, centre of gravity and operating characteristics.

objects.name: roof mechanical-equipment support frame
objects.definition: A raised metal frame or proprietary roof stand that carries a mechanical unit above a roof and transfers its loads to designated structural supports.
functions: Maintain level on a pitched or flat roof
Provide clearance for roofing, flashing, drainage and maintenance

cad.pattern: One braced frame under each roof-mounted unit
cad.placement: Above roof with legs or rails aligned to structural supports
cad.start: Roof structure and flashed fixing points
cad.opening: Coordinates roof penetrations without obstructing drainage
cad.load: Transfers equipment, vibration and wind actions into roof structure

notes: The frame requires structural and weatherproofing design specific to the roof and equipment.

objects.name: suspended mechanical-equipment hanger rod
objects.definition: A threaded steel rod and associated nuts, washers and brackets suspending a mechanical unit or support frame from overhead structure.
materials: zinc-plated or galvanised threaded steel rod
attributes: seismic or wind restraint where applicable

cad.pattern: Four or more vertical rods at equipment or frame fixing points
cad.placement: Between overhead structure and concealed mechanical unit
cad.end: Equipment bracket, angle or support frame
cad.opening: Passes through ceiling space without loading ceiling grid
cad.load: Axial tension transfers equipment weight to structure

notes: Hanger rods must connect to structure, not simply to ceiling lining or grid.

objects.name: mechanical-equipment service platform
objects.definition: A permanent platform, deck or framed shelf supporting mechanical equipment and sometimes providing a maintained access surface around it.
functions: Support safe documented maintenance access where required

cad.pattern: One platform under or beside selected plant
cad.placement: Roof space, plant cupboard, roof or external service area
cad.opening: Coordinates service penetrations and drain routes
cad.load: Transfers equipment, personnel and maintenance loads to structure

notes: Access and fall-protection requirements are project-specific and are not satisfied by a platform outline alone.

objects.name: mechanical air duct
objects.definition: A closed passage made from flexible or rigid construction that carries supply, return, outdoor or exhaust air as part of a mechanical air-distribution system.
functions: Convey air between equipment and terminals
Provide a sealable and supportable route through the building

ncc_references.relationship: Heating and cooling ducts and fittings require specified insulation and sealing unless an exclusion applies.

cad.pattern: Continuous routed segments between fittings and terminals
cad.placement: Ceiling, roof, wall, floor, bulkhead or plant service zones
cad.opening: Passes through coordinated sleeves or framed openings
cad.load: Duct self-weight and air-pressure forces carried by supports

notes: Air purpose must be stored explicitly; a supply duct is not interchangeable with contaminated-air exhaust simply because the geometry matches.

objects.name: insulated flexible air duct
objects.definition: A factory-made bendable circular duct with a flexible inner air core, surrounding thermal insulation and an outer jacket, commonly supplied in compressed lengths for residential systems.
functions: Provide an integrated insulated duct run
materials: laminated polymer or foil inner core

ncc_references.relationship: Flexible heating and cooling ductwork is subject to insulation and draw-band plus sealant or tape sealing provisions.

cad.pattern: Smooth routed curves between circular spigots with supported sag limits
cad.placement: Commonly through residential roof and ceiling spaces
cad.start: Upstream spigot and sealed draw band
cad.end: Downstream spigot and sealed draw band
cad.opening: Requires clear route without crushing or sharp bends
cad.load: Duct supported by broad straps or saddles without compressing insulation

notes: Nominal R-value and installed performance are not interchangeable when insulation is compressed, wet or discontinuous.

objects.name: flexible-duct inner core
objects.definition: The air-carrying flexible tube inside insulated flexible duct, formed from a reinforced laminated membrane around a helical wire or similar support.

cad.pattern: Helically reinforced flexible tube following duct centreline
cad.placement: Innermost air passage of flexible duct
cad.opening: Internal bore remains extended and uncrushed
cad.load: Air pressure and light tension carried by reinforced membrane; external straps support complete duct

notes: Nude core can be sold separately, but it does not provide the thermal performance of insulated flexible duct.

objects.name: flexible-duct thermal insulation
objects.definition: The annular bulk-insulation layer surrounding the inner core of insulated flexible duct.
functions: Reduce heat transfer through duct wall
Help limit condensation on cooling ducts
Fill the space between inner core and outer jacket

ncc_references.relationship: Duct insulation must achieve the applicable material R-value and remain continuous and in position.

cad.pattern: Concentric insulation layer following flexible inner core
cad.placement: Between inner core and outer jacket
cad.opening: Continuous around core except controlled connection zones
cad.load: Non-structural layer protected from compression and moisture

notes: The explanatory insulation thickness examples in the NCC are not universal product dimensions.

objects.name: flexible-duct outer jacket
objects.definition: The flexible outer sleeve enclosing and protecting the thermal insulation of insulated flexible duct.
functions: Provide a vapour and weather-control surface where declared
Protect insulation from handling and minor moisture exposure

ncc_references.relationship: An outer protective sleeve and sealed protective sheeting are required for specified exposed duct locations.

cad.pattern: Flexible concentric membrane following insulated duct
cad.placement: Outermost factory jacket of flexible duct
cad.opening: Closes over insulation and is taped at connections
cad.load: Non-structural protective layer supported with complete duct

notes: Not every factory jacket is suitable for prolonged sunlight or exposed weather.

objects.name: rigid circular air duct
objects.definition: A rigid round duct made from spiral-lock, longitudinal-seam or moulded sections used to carry mechanical air.
functions: Convey air in a stable circular passage
Provide a durable supportable duct route

ncc_references.relationship: Rigid heating and cooling ductwork is subject to specified material R-value and Class C air sealing.

cad.pattern: Straight cylindrical segments joined by couplings and fittings
cad.placement: Plant rooms, ceiling spaces, exposed interiors or service shafts
cad.opening: Maintains full round bore through supported route
cad.load: Duct weight and pressure forces carried by hangers, saddles or brackets

notes: Spiral duct is one manufacturing form, not a synonym for every round rigid duct.

objects.name: rectangular sheet-metal air duct
objects.definition: A rigid rectangular duct formed from sheet metal with longitudinal seams, transverse joints and reinforcement suited to its size and pressure.
functions: Convey air in a rectangular passage
Fit within shallow or coordinated service zones
Connect rectangular equipment, plenums and fittings

ncc_references.relationship: Rigid heating and cooling ductwork is subject to specified material R-value and Class C air sealing.

cad.pattern: Straight rectangular segments joined at transverse flanges or slip joints
cad.placement: Ceiling, bulkhead, plant or shaft service zones
cad.opening: Maintains full rectangular bore through route
cad.load: Duct weight and pressure loads transferred through trapezes or brackets

objects.name: pre-insulated rigid duct panel
objects.definition: A rigid insulation board or composite panel faced with vapour-control and protective layers and fabricated into rectangular duct or fittings.
functions: Create lightweight rectangular duct sections and fittings
materials: rigid phenolic, polyurethane or mineral-fibre board

ncc_references.relationship: Rigid duct and its insulation must meet the applicable sealing and thermal path.

cad.pattern: Folded or joined rectangular panels forming duct walls
cad.placement: Ceiling, roof or plant service route
cad.opening: Faced panel encloses continuous air passage
cad.load: Lightweight duct supported by straps or channels without crushing panel

notes: Product facings, fire properties, pressure capability and cleaning suitability require selected-product evidence.

objects.name: internal duct liner
objects.definition: An insulation and acoustic-absorption layer fixed to the inside face of rigid ductwork or a plenum and exposed to the air stream through a suitable facing.
functions: Protect the metal duct wall from internal temperature difference

ncc_references.relationship: Internal insulation can contribute to duct material R-value when installed continuously and in position.

cad.pattern: Continuous lining panels on selected internal duct faces
cad.placement: Inside rigid duct, plenum or silencer
cad.opening: Reduces internal clear duct dimensions
cad.load: Adhesive and pins retain liner against airflow and gravity

notes: Internal dimensions and free area must be based on the lined, not bare, duct.

objects.name: external rigid-duct insulation
objects.definition: A continuous thermal-insulation layer fitted around the outside of rigid ductwork and fittings.
functions: Provide the required material R-value around ducts and fittings

ncc_references.relationship: Duct insulation must achieve applicable material R-value, abut adjoining insulation and maintain its position and thickness.

cad.pattern: Continuous rectangular or cylindrical layer around rigid duct and fittings
cad.placement: Outside rigid duct surfaces
cad.opening: Wraps around joints and fittings while preserving access where designed
cad.load: Non-structural layer held by facing, pins, bands or jacket

notes: Supports and flanges may locally interrupt thickness, but the broader barrier must remain continuous as required.

objects.name: cooling-duct vapour barrier
objects.definition: A continuous low-permeance facing, jacket or sealed membrane on the warm side of cooling-duct insulation that limits water-vapour entry into the insulation.
functions: Limit vapour diffusion into cold insulation
Reduce interstitial and surface condensation risk
Provide a sealable outer layer at joints and penetrations

ncc_references.relationship: Explanatory guidance notes that refrigerated-cooling duct insulation should have a vapour barrier to prevent condensation damage.

cad.pattern: Continuous sealed membrane around cooling-duct insulation
cad.placement: Outside insulation on refrigerated supply and return ducts where required
cad.opening: Sealed around hangers, fittings and service penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural membrane supported by insulation and jacket

notes: Vapour-control continuity is a relationship and evidence field, not only a material name.

objects.name: exposed-duct protective jacket
objects.definition: A weather-resistant outer sheeting or sleeve enclosing duct insulation in an exposed, underfloor, attached-garage or roof-space location where protection from damp is required.
functions: Protect insulation from water and physical damage
Provide a taped airtight and waterproof outer surface

ncc_references.relationship: Duct insulation in nominated locations requires an outer sleeve of protective sheeting sealed with adhesive tape at least 48 mm wide.

cad.pattern: Continuous outer layer around insulated duct and fittings
cad.placement: Outside building, under suspended floor, attached Class 10a space or roof space as applicable
cad.opening: Taped around all seams and penetrations
cad.load: Protective layer supported by duct and insulation

notes: The NCC minimum tape width is a rule attribute; the actual installed tape remains a separate physical object below.

objects.name: rigid-duct longitudinal seam
objects.definition: A folded, locked, welded or otherwise joined longitudinal edge connection closing a sheet-metal duct section along its length.
functions: Provide a sealable continuous longitudinal joint

ncc_references.relationship: Openings, joints and seams in heating and cooling duct surfaces require Class C sealing.

cad.pattern: Continuous seam along each fabricated sheet-metal section
cad.placement: Along duct wall parallel to airflow
cad.opening: Closes joined sheet edges
cad.load: Carries local sheet and pressure forces

objects.name: rigid-duct transverse joint
objects.definition: A flange, slip, socket, coupling or proprietary joint connecting adjacent rigid duct sections across the airflow direction.
functions: Provide a gasketed or sealed demountable or permanent connection

ncc_references.relationship: Duct joints require the applicable Class C air sealing.

cad.pattern: One perimeter joint between each pair of rigid duct sections
cad.placement: Across duct at fabrication and installation module boundaries
cad.opening: Maintains full air passage through aligned sections
cad.load: Transfers local duct alignment and pressure loads; supports remain independent

objects.name: duct sealant or mastic
objects.definition: A compatible brush-, gun- or bead-applied sealing compound used at duct seams, joints, fittings and penetrations to limit air leakage.
functions: Bridge small gaps at joints and seams
Remain adhered under duct temperature and pressure conditions

ncc_references.relationship: Adhesives, mastics, sealants or gaskets may close duct openings, joints and seams for Class C sealing.

cad.pattern: Continuous bead or coated strip along selected leakage paths
cad.placement: At duct seams, joints, corners, fittings and penetrations
cad.opening: Closes gaps without obstructing air passage
cad.load: Non-structural flexible seal follows joint movement

notes: Sealant selection and workmanship determine performance; a coloured line in the model is not verification.

objects.name: duct sealing tape
objects.definition: A pressure-sensitive adhesive tape selected to seal flexible-duct jackets, protective sheeting, insulation facings or compatible duct joints.
functions: Secure selected connection layers with compatible adhesive
materials: polymer cloth tape approved for use

ncc_references.relationship: Flexible-duct connections may use sealant or adhesive tape with a draw band; protective outer sleeves require not less than 48 mm wide adhesive tape.

cad.pattern: One or more circumferential wraps or linear strips over each selected closure
cad.placement: At flexible-duct connections, insulation and protective-jacket seams
cad.end: Overlap beyond joint or around full circumference
cad.opening: Conforms to substrate without wrinkles or unsealed edges
cad.load: Adhesive seal only; not the sole structural duct support

notes: The everyday term duct tape is too broad; compatibility and intended use must be explicit.

objects.name: flexible-duct draw band
objects.definition: A tensioned band or heavy-duty tie around flexible duct inner core at a spigot, used with sealant or compatible tape to retain and seal the connection.
functions: Clamp flexible core to a spigot
Compress the core over the sealed connection surface

ncc_references.relationship: Flexible ductwork may be sealed with a draw band in conjunction with sealant or adhesive tape.

cad.pattern: One circumferential band around each flexible inner-core connection
cad.placement: Over inner core on circular spigot behind retaining bead where provided
cad.opening: Clamps without puncturing or cutting core
cad.load: Carries connection pull-off force, not duct self-weight

notes: The outer jacket normally needs its own separate closure after the core connection is completed.

objects.name: duct connection gasket
objects.definition: A compressible strip, ring or moulded seal between mating duct flanges, equipment faces or fitting connections.
functions: Permit demountable bolted or clipped connections

ncc_references.relationship: Gaskets are one stated means of closing duct openings, joints and seams for Class C sealing.

cad.pattern: Continuous ring or perimeter strip at each selected mating face
cad.placement: Between duct flanges, panels or equipment connection faces
cad.opening: Surrounds air passage without projecting into bore
cad.load: Compressed between connected faces

objects.name: duct collar or spigot
objects.definition: A short circular or rectangular neck fixed to equipment, a plenum, duct or terminal box to receive a connected duct.
functions: Receive flexible core, coupling, gasket or flange

cad.pattern: One projecting neck at each duct connection point
cad.placement: On equipment casing, plenum, main duct, fitting or terminal box
cad.opening: Maintains full connection bore
cad.load: Transfers connection forces to host; duct separately supported

notes: Collar and spigot overlap in Australian trade usage; store the actual fixing and shape.

objects.name: circular duct coupling
objects.definition: A short male, female or sleeved fitting joining two circular duct sections of the same nominal size.
functions: Provide surfaces for bands, screws and seals

cad.pattern: One short coaxial fitting between equal-size duct ends
cad.placement: At inline duct section joins
cad.opening: Maintains circular air bore
cad.load: Joint alignment only; adjacent duct supports carry weight

objects.name: circular duct elbow
objects.definition: A curved or segmented circular fitting that changes the direction of a round duct route.
functions: Connect straight duct sections at a selected angle

cad.pattern: One curved fitting at each discrete circular route change
cad.placement: Between straight duct segments or at equipment and plenums
cad.opening: Maintains circular bore through bend
cad.load: Fitting supported with adjacent duct and separately where required

notes: A tight kink in flexible duct is not a modelled elbow and can seriously alter airflow.

objects.name: rectangular duct elbow
objects.definition: A fabricated rectangular fitting that changes duct direction, with a radius, square throat, turning vanes or other documented internal geometry.
functions: Manage pressure loss and air distribution through the turn

cad.pattern: One fabricated fitting at each rectangular route turn
cad.placement: Between straight rectangular duct sections
cad.opening: Maintains designed internal turn geometry
cad.load: Fitting supported from adjacent duct or dedicated trapeze

notes: Turning vanes are separate internal physical parts when present, not a universal elbow feature.

objects.name: duct tee fitting
objects.definition: A three-way fitting with a main air passage and a branch generally meeting at or near a right angle.
functions: Connect a branch to a main duct

cad.pattern: One three-way fitting at each tee branch node
cad.placement: Within main or branch duct route
cad.end: Downstream main and side branch connections
cad.opening: Three continuous air passages
cad.load: Supported with adjacent ducts and dedicated support where needed

objects.name: duct wye fitting
objects.definition: A three-way Y-shaped fitting that divides or combines airflow through two angled branches.
functions: Divide a main air stream into two branches
Provide a smoother branch angle than a square tee where selected

cad.pattern: One Y-shaped fitting at each two-branch division
cad.placement: Within circular or compatible duct route
cad.opening: Three continuous air passages
cad.load: Fitting and branches separately supported

objects.name: duct reducer
objects.definition: A tapered or stepped fitting connecting ducts of the same general shape but different sizes.

cad.pattern: One tapered fitting at each same-shape size change
cad.placement: Between unequal duct segments or equipment spigot and duct
cad.opening: Internal area changes through taper
cad.load: Supported with adjacent duct sections

notes: Airflow direction does not always run from large to small; the fitting name describes geometry.

objects.name: duct shape transition
objects.definition: A fabricated fitting changing duct cross-section between circular, oval, square or rectangular shapes and possibly between unequal sizes.
functions: Connect different duct or equipment connection shapes
Coordinate duct geometry through a constrained route

cad.pattern: One lofted fitting between unlike duct or equipment faces
cad.placement: At equipment, plenums or route shape changes
cad.opening: Internal passage morphs between shapes
cad.load: Transition independently supported where equipment faces must remain unloaded

objects.name: duct branch take-off fitting
objects.definition: A collar, shoe or formed fitting fixed to a main duct opening to start a branch duct.
functions: Connect a branch to a main duct
Provide a spigot or flange for branch connection and optional damper
not_synonyms: plain spigot not connected to main

cad.pattern: One fitting at each cut branch opening in a main duct
cad.placement: On side, top or bottom of main rigid duct or plenum
cad.opening: Penetrates main duct wall with shaped entry
cad.load: Take-off fixed to main duct; branch independently supported

objects.name: insulated duct splitter fitting
objects.definition: A multi-outlet insulated fitting that divides airflow from one fan-coil or main duct connection into two or more branch ducts and may accept balancing or motorised dampers.
functions: Provide a sealed insulated distribution node
materials: moulded polymer or insulated metal body

cad.pattern: One central body with two or more numbered radial or axial outlets
cad.placement: Close to ducted fan coil or main distribution point
cad.opening: Internal chamber distributes air to outlets
cad.load: Fitting independently suspended or supported; branches separately strapped

notes: Diffusion fitting is Australian trade language for a particular multi-outlet product family, not every airflow diffuser.

objects.name: supply-air plenum
objects.definition: A chamber attached to the supply side of mechanical equipment or a distribution point that receives conditioned air and feeds one or more duct outlets.
functions: Provide connection faces for transitions, spigots and dampers
not_synonyms: ceiling void used informally as plenum

cad.pattern: One chamber immediately downstream of fan coil or at major distribution node
cad.placement: At equipment discharge in ceiling or plant space
cad.opening: Encloses a common supply-air volume
cad.load: Independently suspended so equipment casing carries no duct weight

notes: Using an unsealed ceiling void as a supply plenum is not implied by this object.

objects.name: return-air plenum
objects.definition: A chamber on the return side of mechanical equipment that collects air from one or more return paths and delivers it to the filter and indoor unit.
functions: Connect return grilles or ducts to equipment
House or connect filters and access panels where designed
not_synonyms: roof-space void used as return path automatically

cad.pattern: One chamber immediately upstream of fan coil or at return collection node
cad.placement: At equipment intake or behind return-air grille
cad.opening: Encloses a common return-air volume with service access
cad.load: Independently suspended or supported

notes: Return-air leakage can draw roof-space contaminants; the route and enclosure must be explicit.

objects.name: supply-air terminal box
objects.definition: A small plenum box connecting a branch duct to a ceiling, wall or floor supply outlet.
functions: Adapt duct shape and size to the outlet neck
Distribute air across the outlet face
Provide a supported sealed connection behind the finish surface

cad.pattern: One box behind each supply grille or diffuser requiring a plenum
cad.placement: Above ceiling, behind wall or below floor outlet
cad.opening: Occupies outlet cut-out and seals to terminal
cad.load: Box and outlet independently supported from lining where required

objects.name: return-air box
objects.definition: A box behind a return-air grille that connects the grille face to one or more return ducts and may hold a filter frame.
functions: Collect room air through the grille
Connect the grille to return ductwork
Support or seal a removable filter where designed

cad.pattern: One box behind each ducted return-air grille
cad.placement: Above ceiling or behind wall return opening
cad.opening: Aligns with finished return opening
cad.load: Box and grille supported by frame or structure, not loose ceiling lining

objects.name: linear-slot diffuser cushion-head box
objects.definition: A long shallow plenum box behind a linear-slot diffuser that receives one or more round or rectangular ducts and distributes air along the slot length.
functions: Equalise air along a linear diffuser
Adapt branch ducts to a long narrow outlet
Accept a balancing damper at the inlet where selected

cad.pattern: One elongated box following each linear diffuser segment
cad.placement: Above ceiling or behind wall slot diffuser
cad.start: One or more duct inlet spigots
cad.opening: Distributes air across long narrow outlet
cad.load: Box and diffuser independently supported at selected points

notes: Cushion head is established Australian diffuser trade terminology and is unrelated to soft furnishings.

objects.name: flexible equipment-to-duct connector
objects.definition: A short flexible fabric or elastomeric connection between vibrating mechanical equipment and rigid ductwork or a plenum.
functions: Accommodate small movement and alignment differences
Maintain a sealed air passage between equipment and duct

cad.pattern: One short flexible perimeter section at selected equipment connection
cad.placement: Between unit casing and independently supported duct or plenum
cad.opening: Forms continuous flexible air passage
cad.load: Carries air pressure only; duct weight remains independently supported

notes: Canvas is legacy trade language; modern connector materials and fire properties require product evidence.

objects.name: duct access door
objects.definition: A framed removable or hinged door in a duct or plenum that allows inspection, cleaning or service of internal components.
functions: Close and seal the access opening during operation
Permit maintenance of dampers, coils, filters or drains

cad.pattern: One door beside each selected internal maintained component or cleaning zone
cad.placement: On accessible side of rigid duct or plenum
cad.opening: Door clears surrounding services when opened
cad.load: Door carried by frame; frame reinforced into duct wall

notes: The working space outside the door is analysis metadata, not part of the door solid.

objects.name: manual volume-control damper
objects.definition: A manually set blade or blade set within a duct or fitting that throttles airflow for branch balancing.
functions: Provide an accessible operating shaft or quadrant

cad.pattern: One damper blade or set at selected branch take-offs and terminal inlets
cad.placement: In accessible duct or fitting with operating quadrant outside insulation
cad.opening: Blade rotates within air passage
cad.load: Damper frame supported by duct; shaft carries operating torque

notes: A balancing setting is commissioning data, not a separate physical part.

objects.name: motorised zone damper
objects.definition: A duct damper fitted with an electric actuator that opens, closes or modulates airflow to a controlled room zone.
functions: Provide position or end-switch feedback where fitted

cad.pattern: One actuator-equipped damper at each controlled zone branch
cad.placement: Accessible duct branch near main distribution point
cad.opening: Blade rotates or translates within duct
cad.load: Damper body supported by duct and actuator carried by shaft frame

notes: Closed, minimum-open and modulating behaviour are control attributes, not inferable from the damper shape.

objects.name: duct-damper actuator
objects.definition: An electric motor or thermal drive attached to a damper shaft or linkage to move the blade in response to a control signal.
functions: Hold or return the selected position
Provide position feedback or end switching where fitted

cad.pattern: One compact actuator on each motorised damper shaft
cad.placement: Outside duct insulation at accessible branch location
cad.opening: Requires rotation and replacement clearance
cad.load: Actuator weight and torque carried by damper frame

objects.name: rectangular-duct turning vane
objects.definition: A curved internal blade within a rectangular duct elbow that guides airflow through a sharp change in direction.
functions: Distribute flow across the elbow passage

cad.pattern: Repeated curved blades spanning an elbow width
cad.placement: Inside selected square or short-radius rectangular elbow
cad.opening: Divides air passage into guided channels
cad.load: Air forces transferred through vane rails to elbow walls

notes: Only model vanes where the selected fitting includes them.

objects.name: supply-air grille
objects.definition: A framed room terminal with fixed or adjustable bars or blades through which mechanically supplied air enters a space.
functions: Protect the branch opening while preserving free area

cad.pattern: One grille at each scheduled supply opening
cad.placement: Ceiling, high wall, low wall or other designed room surface
cad.end: Visible blade face and room air pattern
cad.opening: Occupies framed finish opening
cad.load: Grille supported by terminal box, frame or substrate
