objects.name: supply-air register
objects.definition: A supply-air grille combined with an integral or directly attached volume-control damper.

cad.pattern: One dampered terminal at selected supply opening
cad.placement: Wall, ceiling or floor according to register type
cad.start: Duct or box neck and damper
cad.opening: Occupies finish opening with accessible adjustment
cad.load: Supported by box, frame or substrate

notes: In everyday Australian usage register and grille can be blurred; the ontology reserves register for a terminal with airflow control.

objects.name: ceiling air diffuser
objects.definition: A ceiling-mounted supply terminal shaped to distribute air across one or more directions with a designed spread and induction pattern.
functions: Spread supply air into a room

cad.pattern: One diffuser at each scheduled ceiling supply point
cad.placement: Flush, lay-in or surface mounted in ceiling
cad.opening: Occupies ceiling cut-out or grid module
cad.load: Diffuser and box supported independently where required

objects.name: round ceiling air diffuser
objects.definition: A circular ceiling diffuser with concentric cones, a disc or adjustable central element that spreads supply air radially or in a selected pattern.
functions: Distribute air from a circular branch
Adjust flow or pattern where the centre is movable

cad.pattern: One circular terminal at each selected ceiling point
cad.placement: Ceiling connected to circular branch or box
cad.opening: Occupies round ceiling opening
cad.load: Supported by spigot, box or ceiling frame as selected

notes: Disc valve is not a safe synonym for every round supply diffuser because many disc valves are used for exhaust.

objects.name: multi-directional ceiling outlet
objects.definition: A square or rectangular ceiling supply diffuser with individually adjustable blades or segments that direct air in several selected directions.
functions: Distribute supply air across multiple directions

cad.pattern: One square outlet with configurable directional segments at each point
cad.placement: Ceiling supply location
cad.opening: Occupies square or rectangular ceiling cut-out
cad.load: Supported by box or ceiling frame

notes: MDO is common Australian HVAC trade terminology and should be searchable directly.

objects.name: linear-slot air diffuser
objects.definition: A long narrow supply or return terminal with one or more slots and, on supply models, internal pattern controllers that direct air along the ceiling or into the room.
functions: Distribute air through a narrow architectural opening
Provide adjustable directional pattern where fitted

cad.pattern: Individual modules or continuous aligned runs
cad.placement: Ceiling, bulkhead edge or high wall
cad.end: Last module, end cap or mitred corner
cad.opening: Occupies long narrow finish opening connected to box
cad.load: Diffuser and cushion head supported at designed intervals

notes: A linear slot can be configured for supply or return; air-path purpose must be explicit.

objects.name: double-deflection supply grille
objects.definition: A wall or duct-mounted supply grille with two banks of adjustable blades, usually oriented at right angles to provide horizontal and vertical air-direction control.
functions: Direct supply air in two axes
Finish a wall or duct opening

cad.pattern: One two-layer blade panel at selected supply opening
cad.placement: High wall, sidewall or exposed duct face
cad.opening: Occupies framed opening
cad.load: Grille fixed to box, duct or wall frame

objects.name: floor supply register
objects.definition: A load-resistant floor-mounted supply grille, commonly with adjustable blades or a damper, connected to underfloor ductwork or a floor terminal box.
functions: Deliver supply air from below the floor
Allow local direction or flow adjustment where fitted

cad.pattern: One flush grille in each selected floor supply opening
cad.placement: Finished floor above underfloor duct or box
cad.opening: Occupies trimmed floor opening
cad.load: Foot traffic carried through grille frame to floor structure

notes: Floor vent is broad everyday language and can also mean subfloor ventilation.

objects.name: return-air grille
objects.definition: A large framed grille through which room air enters a return-air box, plenum or duct on its way back to mechanical equipment.
functions: Provide a removable face or access path where designed

cad.pattern: One or more large grilles at selected central or distributed return points
cad.placement: Ceiling, wall or floor with clear air path
cad.opening: Occupies framed return opening
cad.load: Grille and box supported by frame or structure

notes: Furniture and doors can obstruct a correctly sized grille; placement clearance is instance data.

objects.name: filter return-air grille
objects.definition: A hinged or removable return-air grille assembly with rails, clips or a frame holding a replaceable or washable air filter behind the visible face.
functions: Provide routine filter removal and replacement access

cad.pattern: One hinged filter grille at selected return point
cad.placement: Ceiling or wall with full filter removal clearance
cad.opening: Grille swings or removes without obstruction
cad.load: Frame carries grille and filter to structure or box

notes: Filter dimensions and maintenance clearance must be stored; a nominal grille face size is insufficient.

objects.name: mechanical outdoor-air intake terminal
objects.definition: A weather-protected wall or roof hood, louvre or cowl where a mechanical ventilation duct draws outdoor air into the building.
functions: Limit rain, debris and pest entry
Connect the external opening to the intake duct

cad.pattern: One intake terminal per outdoor-air duct path
cad.placement: External wall or roof away from documented contamination and exhaust sources
cad.opening: Penetrates envelope with flashed and sealed flange
cad.load: Terminal supported by wall, roof or independent duct frame

notes: Intake separation distances and contamination risk are design analysis, not fixed geometry defaults.

objects.name: mechanical-ventilation outdoor exhaust terminal
objects.definition: A weather-protected wall or roof hood, louvre or cowl where mechanical ventilation ductwork discharges air outdoors.
functions: Limit rain and pest entry when not operating
Connect exhaust duct to the envelope opening

cad.pattern: One exhaust terminal per independent discharge path
cad.placement: External wall or roof with designed separation from intakes and openings
cad.opening: Penetrates envelope with flashed and sealed flange
cad.load: Terminal supported by wall, roof or duct frame

notes: This generic ventilation terminal overlaps physically with domestic exhaust terminals but remains tied to a different system path and separation analysis.

objects.name: mechanical air-terminal pest screen
objects.definition: A corrosion-resistant mesh or grille layer across an outdoor air terminal that limits entry by insects, birds or small animals while preserving designed airflow.
functions: Remain removable or accessible for cleaning

cad.pattern: One mesh field across selected external terminal throat
cad.placement: Within intake or exhaust hood behind weather protection
cad.opening: Apertures preserve documented net free area
cad.load: Mesh and debris loads transferred to terminal frame

notes: A generic pest screen must not be claimed as bushfire-compliant ember protection without selected evidence.

objects.name: duct silencer
objects.definition: A lined or baffled duct section designed to reduce sound travelling along an air path while allowing airflow through it.
functions: Limit room-to-room sound transfer through ducts

cad.pattern: One enlarged or lined inline section at selected noise-control location
cad.placement: Between fan or equipment and noise-sensitive duct branches or terminals
cad.opening: Straight or baffled internal air passages
cad.load: Silencer independently suspended due to concentrated weight

notes: Acoustic performance is frequency-dependent product data and is not established by length alone.

objects.name: duct airflow test port
objects.definition: A small sealed opening, plug or nipple in ductwork that permits insertion of a pressure, temperature or airflow measuring probe.
functions: Reseal the duct after probe removal

cad.pattern: Discrete sealed ports at selected upstream and downstream test locations
cad.placement: Accessible rigid duct or plenum face
cad.opening: Reseals after measurement
cad.load: Light fitting supported by reinforced duct wall

notes: Measurement results are evidence linked to the port, not geometry.

objects.name: flexible-duct support strap
objects.definition: A broad strap or sling supporting insulated flexible duct from structure without crushing the insulation or sharply deforming the air core.
functions: Maintain the designed route and cross-section
materials: galvanised metal strap with protective width

cad.pattern: Repeated broad slings beneath flexible duct at designed intervals
cad.placement: Suspended from roof or ceiling structure
cad.opening: Cradle follows duct without pinching
cad.load: Transfers duct and insulation weight to structure

notes: A narrow tie can damage or constrict flexible duct and should not be substituted for a support strap.

objects.name: rigid-duct trapeze support
objects.definition: A horizontal channel or angle beneath rigid duct, suspended by two or more rods from structure to form a trapeze support.
functions: Distribute support load across duct width
Provide adjustable elevation and coordinated support for services

cad.pattern: Repeated horizontal channels beneath rigid duct with paired vertical rods
cad.placement: Suspended from overhead structure
cad.opening: Maintains insulation thickness or uses load-spreading inserts
cad.load: Transfers duct, insulation and pressure loads to structure

notes: Unistrut is proprietary language often used generically for slotted support channel.

objects.name: duct-support threaded rod
objects.definition: A vertical threaded steel rod connecting a duct trapeze, ring hanger or bracket to an overhead structural anchor.

cad.pattern: Paired or repeated vertical rods at each trapeze or ring hanger
cad.placement: Between structure and duct support
cad.opening: Passes through service zone without fouling access
cad.load: Axial tension transfers duct load to structure

objects.name: circular-duct ring hanger
objects.definition: A split ring, band or saddle that surrounds or cradles rigid circular duct and connects it to a rod or bracket support.
functions: Transfer duct weight to hanger rod or bracket

cad.pattern: Repeated rings or saddles around circular duct
cad.placement: At designed support points connected to rods or wall brackets
cad.opening: Surrounds duct without crushing insulation
cad.load: Transfers circular duct load to support

objects.name: duct wall-support bracket
objects.definition: A cantilever, angle or framed bracket anchored to a wall to support horizontal or vertical ductwork.
functions: Provide attachment for saddles, channels or restraints
materials: galvanised or stainless steel angle or channel

cad.pattern: Repeated wall brackets beneath or beside duct route
cad.placement: Anchored to structural wall or frame
cad.opening: Maintains clearance for insulation and access
cad.load: Transfers duct weight and restraint loads into wall structure

objects.name: ducted HVAC zone controller
objects.definition: A fixed user interface and control processor that manages room zones, sensors and motorised dampers in a ducted heating or cooling system.
functions: Command dampers and communicate with the HVAC unit

cad.pattern: One primary wall controller with optional secondary controllers
cad.placement: Accessible occupied-space wall
cad.opening: Wall box or cable penetration
cad.load: Light fixture load carried by wall fixings

notes: Cloud services and software screens are not physical objects; only installed controllers and gateways are modelled.

objects.name: HVAC zone temperature sensor
objects.definition: A wall, ceiling or controller-integrated sensor that measures temperature in a controlled HVAC zone and sends it to the zone or equipment controller.
functions: Represent temperature demand away from the main controller where required

cad.pattern: One or more sensors per controlled zone
cad.placement: Representative room position away from misleading heat and drafts
cad.opening: May require small cable penetration
cad.load: Light device fixed to wall or ceiling

notes: A sensor location is part of the control design; placing it at an arbitrary convenient wall can distort operation.

objects.name: HVAC Wi-Fi control gateway
objects.definition: A fixed interface module that links compatible mechanical equipment or a zone controller to a local wireless network for remote monitoring and commands.
functions: Bridge HVAC control communications to Wi-Fi
Expose selected status and settings to an app or network service

cad.pattern: One gateway per compatible unit, controller or system group
cad.placement: Inside or adjacent to equipment or controller with usable radio path
cad.opening: Requires cable and service access
cad.load: Light module clipped or screwed to equipment or nearby substrate

notes: The wireless network and cloud service are non-physical relationships; the gateway is the installed object.

objects.name: ventilation carbon-dioxide sensor
objects.definition: A fixed indoor sensor that measures carbon-dioxide concentration as an occupancy-related input to compatible mechanical-ventilation controls.
materials: optical or other CO2 sensing element

cad.pattern: One or more sensors in representative occupied zones
cad.placement: Wall or return-air position according to selected design
cad.opening: Sensor grille remains exposed to room air
cad.load: Light device fixed to wall, ceiling or duct

notes: CO2 is not carbon monoxide; the object must never be substituted for a life-safety CO alarm.

objects.name: ventilation humidity sensor
objects.definition: A fixed sensor that measures relative humidity and provides an input to ventilation, exhaust or dehumidification controls.
functions: Boost or reduce ventilation according to control logic

cad.pattern: One sensor in selected moisture-generating or representative zone
cad.placement: Wall, ceiling, return air or equipment according to control design
cad.opening: Sensor vents remain unobstructed
cad.load: Light device fixed to substrate or equipment

notes: A humidistat contains control logic; a humidity sensor may only report a value.

objects.name: packaged ducted evaporative cooler
objects.definition: A factory-made outdoor-air cooling unit containing wetted media, a water system and a fan, connected to a building supply-air duct system.
functions: Draw outdoor air through wetted media
Deliver cooled air into supply ductwork

cad.pattern: One packaged unit per selected house or mechanical zone
cad.placement: Usually on a roof support, platform or external plant position
cad.start: Outdoor-air intake faces and water/power connections
cad.opening: Requires unobstructed intake faces, service access and roof penetration
cad.load: Wet operating mass, wind and vibration transferred through dedicated support

notes: Model the selected manufacturer's casing and connection geometry; nominal catalogue dimensions are not universal.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler cabinet
objects.definition: The weather-exposed enclosure, structural shell and removable access faces surrounding a packaged evaporative cooler's internal parts.
functions: Protect internal components while permitting service access

cad.pattern: One cabinet around each packaged cooler
cad.placement: At external cooler location
cad.opening: Intake and service faces remain clear
cad.load: Carries panels and internal mountings into cooler base

notes: The cabinet is an assembly; individual access panels may be instances of the generic mechanical-equipment access panel.

objects.name: evaporative-cooling media panel
objects.definition: A porous replaceable panel kept wet so incoming outdoor air loses sensible heat as some water evaporates.
functions: Present a wetted surface to intake air
Distribute water through the media depth

cad.pattern: Usually one media panel per cabinet intake face
cad.placement: Behind external intake grille or louvred cabinet face
cad.opening: Full panel face remains open to airflow
cad.load: Panel retained by frame and supported at base

notes: Treat it as cooling media, not as a ventilation filter with a declared filtration grade unless product evidence says so.

objects.name: evaporative-media retaining frame
objects.definition: A removable or fixed perimeter frame that locates an evaporative-cooling media panel and maintains its air and water path.

cad.pattern: One frame around each media panel
cad.placement: Within each cooler intake face
cad.opening: Leaves media airflow area unobstructed
cad.load: Transfers media wet weight to cabinet

objects.name: evaporative-cooler water reservoir
objects.definition: The basin or sump in the base of an evaporative cooler that holds recirculating water below the media and pump.
functions: Provide a low point for drain or bleed functions

cad.pattern: One reservoir in the base of each wet cooler
cad.placement: Below media panels and water-distribution system
cad.end: Pump inlet, drain and overflow points
cad.opening: Top is accessible after cabinet panels are removed
cad.load: Water mass carried through cooler base and roof support

notes: Stored water is operational content; the reservoir is the permanent physical object.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler water-circulation pump
objects.definition: A small pump that lifts water from the cooler reservoir to the distribution header above the cooling media.
functions: Supply water to media distribution points

cad.pattern: One circulation pump per cooler water circuit
cad.placement: In or above water reservoir
cad.opening: Pump can be removed through service opening
cad.load: Supported by reservoir bracket, base or submerged mounting

objects.name: evaporative-cooler water-distribution header
objects.definition: A small pipe, manifold or channel that spreads pumped water across the upper edges of evaporative-cooling media panels.
functions: Divide pump flow among media panels
Apply water evenly across media width
Return excess water through media to reservoir

cad.pattern: Header segments follow the top edge of each media panel
cad.placement: Above or within the top of cooling media
cad.opening: Outlets remain aligned and unblocked
cad.load: Light pipe supported by cabinet clips

objects.name: evaporative-cooler float valve
objects.definition: A mechanically operated inlet valve whose float maintains the working water level in an evaporative cooler reservoir.
functions: Stop inlet flow at set level

cad.pattern: One valve per reservoir supplied from mains water
cad.placement: At reservoir sidewall or inlet bracket
cad.opening: Float has unobstructed travel
cad.load: Valve supported by reservoir wall or bracket

notes: Backflow-control components belong to the connected plumbing water service and must be modelled to the selected installation design.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler water-inlet connection
objects.definition: The cooler-side fitting or flexible connection joining the building water supply to the cooler float valve or inlet assembly.
functions: Accommodate the selected pipe and cooler connection

cad.pattern: One inlet connection per cooler
cad.placement: At cooler base or cabinet inlet point
cad.opening: Connection remains accessible without obstructing panels
cad.load: Pipe and hose supported so valve is not strained

notes: The upstream pipe, isolation and backflow arrangement should reuse plumbing-service objects when that catalogue slice is linked.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler drain or bleed valve
objects.definition: A manual or automatic valve that releases reservoir water for draining, cleaning or water-quality bleed control.

cad.pattern: One drain device at reservoir low point
cad.placement: In reservoir base or external drain connection
cad.opening: Valve and strainer remain accessible
cad.load: Supported by reservoir or cooler base without pipe strain

notes: Drain and bleed modes are related but not identical; preserve the selected product's operation as an attribute.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler drain and bleed pipe
objects.definition: A routed pipe carrying dumped, overflow or bleed water away from an evaporative cooler to the selected lawful discharge point.
functions: Protect the roof and building from uncontrolled discharge

cad.pattern: Continuous graded route from cooler drain point
cad.placement: Across roof or through service route to selected discharge
cad.opening: Passes through sleeves or flashings where it penetrates construction
cad.load: Water-filled pipe supported by clips without loading cooler fitting

notes: Do not assume a discharge destination; plumbing, environmental and local requirements determine it.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler blower
objects.definition: The fan wheel and housing that draw air through wet media and force cooled air into the supply duct.
functions: Develop pressure for the duct system
Discharge air into the roof dropper

cad.pattern: One blower within each packaged cooler
cad.placement: Between media intake volume and supply discharge
cad.opening: Fan inlet and discharge remain unobstructed
cad.load: Rotating assembly supported by cooler frame with vibration control

objects.name: evaporative-cooler fan motor
objects.definition: The electric motor that drives an evaporative cooler blower directly or through a belt and pulley arrangement.
functions: Convert electrical energy to fan rotation

cad.pattern: One motor per blower
cad.placement: On blower frame or direct-drive fan hub
cad.opening: Cooling and replacement clearance remains available
cad.load: Motor mass and torque carried by fan frame

objects.name: evaporative-cooler roof dropper duct
objects.definition: A short usually vertical rigid duct passing through the roof zone between a roof-mounted evaporative cooler and the internal supply duct network.
functions: Carry cooled air through the roof
Provide a connection between cooler and ceiling-space ductwork
Coordinate the roof penetration and damper position

ncc_references.relationship: Heating and cooling duct insulation material and exposed-insulation protection.
Heating and cooling ductwork and fittings require specified insulation and sealing unless an exclusion applies.

cad.pattern: One vertical dropper beneath each roof-mounted cooler
cad.placement: Through roof opening into ceiling space
cad.opening: Coordinates with flashed roof opening and structural trimming
cad.load: Independently supported or carried by documented curb; not assumed to support cooler

notes: Whether the dropper carries cooler load is product- and support-design-specific; keep that as an explicit structural attribute.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler duct transition
objects.definition: A rigid tapered fitting changing the cooler or dropper discharge size or shape to match the connected supply-air plenum or duct.
functions: Join different duct sizes or shapes
Guide airflow between cooler and duct network
Provide sealed and insulated connection faces
not_synonyms: generic reducer without selected end geometry

ncc_references.relationship: Heating and cooling duct fittings require specified insulation and sealing unless an exclusion applies.

cad.pattern: One transition where equipment and duct connection geometries differ
cad.placement: Below or beside cooler discharge
cad.opening: Maintains clear internal air path
cad.load: Supported with adjacent rigid duct and isolated from fan vibration where required

objects.name: evaporative-cooler roof support
objects.definition: A proprietary stand, curb or framed support that transfers a roof-mounted evaporative cooler's operating and environmental loads to the building structure.

Transfer gravity, wind and operating loads
Maintain required level, clearance and roof coordination

cad.pattern: One support set beneath each roof cooler
cad.placement: Aligned over documented roof structure and opening
cad.opening: Frames around or integrates the roof penetration
cad.load: Transfers wet mass, wind and vibration to verified structural members

notes: Structural capacity cannot be inferred from geometric contact; store engineering evidence separately.

objects.name: evaporative-cooler roof flashing
objects.definition: A shaped weatherproofing component around the cooler dropper, curb or support penetration where it passes through a roof covering.
functions: Shed roof water around the penetration
Join the equipment opening to roof-covering weatherproofing
Protect cut roof edges and underlay junctions

cad.pattern: One continuous flashing assembly around each roof penetration
cad.placement: Integrated with roof covering around dropper or curb
cad.opening: Closely fits penetration while preserving drainage path
cad.load: Light sheet fixed to roof substrate without supporting equipment

objects.name: evaporative-cooler wall controller
objects.definition: A fixed user control and sensor interface for operating an evaporative cooler's fan, pump, drain cycles and optional automatic modes.
functions: Set fan speed or comfort mode

cad.pattern: One primary controller per cooler or served control zone
cad.placement: Representative internal wall position
cad.end: Control cable or radio link to cooler
cad.opening: Requires small wall-box or cable opening
cad.load: Light fixture fixed to wall

notes: The controller is physical; setpoints, schedules and control logic are data rather than separate building objects.

objects.name: packaged heat-recovery ventilation unit
objects.definition: A fixed mechanical-ventilation unit containing separate supply and extract air paths, fans, filters and an air-to-air heat exchanger in one casing.
functions: Transfer heat between separated air streams

ncc_references.relationship: A mechanical-ventilation system is one path for ventilating a habitable room, sanitary compartment, bathroom, shower room, laundry or other room.

cad.pattern: One central unit with four labelled connections and accessible service face
cad.placement: Ceiling, roof space, plant cupboard or service room
cad.opening: Filter, core and fan access remains usable
cad.load: Unit mass and vibration carried by dedicated hangers, brackets or platform

notes: Never infer the four port roles from position alone; store each selected product's port label and airflow direction.

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation unit casing
objects.definition: The insulated enclosure and internal divider system that holds HRV components and keeps the supply and extract air paths physically separated.
functions: Limit casing heat loss, condensation and air leakage

cad.pattern: One enclosure around each HRV unit
cad.placement: At central ventilation equipment location
cad.opening: Access panels clear internal components
cad.load: Casing transfers internal component mass to mounting points

notes: Use the generic mechanical-equipment access-panel object for separately drawable doors or covers.

objects.name: air-to-air heat-recovery core
objects.definition: A removable heat exchanger containing adjacent but separated passages through which outgoing and incoming air transfer heat without normally mixing.

Keep supply and extract flow passages separated
Reduce ventilation heating or cooling load

cad.placement: Inside HRV casing between filter and fan zones
cad.opening: Core slides out through service face
cad.load: Supported by internal rails and perimeter seals

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation supply fan
objects.definition: The fan inside a balanced ventilation unit that moves outdoor air through the intake, filter and heat-recovery core into the dwelling supply ducts.
functions: Move outdoor air through the supply path

cad.pattern: One supply fan per independent HRV supply path

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation extract fan
objects.definition: The fan inside a balanced ventilation unit that moves stale indoor air through the extract path and heat-recovery core to the outdoor exhaust duct.
functions: Move indoor extract air through the unit
Modulate extract airflow to balance supply

cad.pattern: One extract fan per independent HRV extract path
cad.placement: Inside unit casing on the extract or exhaust side

cad.opening: Fan intake and discharge remain clear
cad.load: Fan frame and isolators carry rotating mass into casing

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation outdoor-air filter
objects.definition: A removable filter panel in the outdoor-air supply path before sensitive unit components or room supply ducts.
functions: Capture particles from incoming outdoor air
Protect the heat-recovery core and supply fan

cad.pattern: One or more filters across the outdoor-air path
cad.placement: Inside unit near outdoor-air intake port
cad.opening: Filter slides out through service face
cad.load: Filter rests in internal rails with perimeter seal

notes: Filter grade is a product property; do not infer it from panel thickness or colour.

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation extract-air filter
objects.definition: A removable filter in the indoor extract-air path that protects the heat-recovery core and extract fan from lint and household dust.
functions: Capture particles from extracted indoor air
Provide a cleanable or replaceable service component

cad.pattern: One or more filters across the indoor extract path
cad.placement: Inside unit near room-extract inlet or core face
cad.opening: Filter slides out through service face
cad.load: Filter rests in internal rails with perimeter seal

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation bypass damper
objects.definition: A motorised or passive air-control blade that diverts one air path around the heat-recovery core when heat exchange is not wanted or when protection logic requires it.

Enable summer bypass or free cooling where designed
Protect or control the core under selected operating conditions

cad.placement: Inside HRV casing beside heat-recovery core
cad.opening: Blade sweep remains clear
cad.load: Damper frame and actuator supported by casing partitions

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation condensate pan
objects.definition: A shallow internal tray that collects water forming or draining below an HRV heat exchanger in units designed for condensate drainage.
functions: Direct water to the unit drain outlet
Protect casing insulation and air paths from uncontrolled water

cad.opening: Pan and outlet can be inspected and cleaned

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation duct port
objects.definition: A flanged, spigotted or socketed unit connection joining one of an HRV's four labelled air paths to its corresponding duct.

cad.placement: On casing faces at manufacturer-defined centres
cad.end: Corresponding supply, extract, intake or exhaust duct
cad.opening: Port bore remains continuous and sealed
cad.load: Duct is independently supported so the port is not overloaded

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation wall controller
objects.definition: A fixed user interface and control device for selecting HRV airflow, operating mode, bypass, schedules and maintenance indications.

cad.pattern: One primary controller with optional secondary inputs
cad.placement: Accessible occupied-space wall
cad.opening: Wall-box or cable penetration
cad.load: Light fixture fixed to wall

notes: Schedules and setpoints are properties of the control record, not physical children.

objects.name: heat-recovery ventilation unit hanging bracket
objects.definition: A manufacturer-provided lug, rail or bracket used with rods or anchors to suspend or fix an HRV unit independently of its ducts.
functions: Connect unit casing to support system
Maintain unit orientation and service position

cad.pattern: Bracket set at manufacturer mounting points
cad.placement: On casing corners, side rails or suspension points
cad.start: Threaded rod, rail, wall or platform support
cad.opening: Does not obstruct service-panel removal
cad.load: Transfers unit mass and operating vibration to verified structure

notes: Duct connections do not support the unit unless a documented design explicitly says they do.

objects.name: hydronic heating distribution pipework assembly
objects.definition: The connected closed-loop flow and return pipe network, including insulation, fittings, supports and distribution components, between a hydronic heat source and its emitters.

Connect pumps, headers, valves and zones
Limit heat loss and permit controlled circulation

ncc_references.relationship: Central-heating water-pipe insulation material and exposed-insulation protection.
Central-heating water-pipe insulation according to pipe location and climate zone.

objects.name: hydronic heating heat-source assembly

objects.definition: A contact, immersion or pocket-mounted sensor that measures hydronic flow, return, tank or mixed-circuit water temperature for control or monitoring.
functions: Provide heat-source, mixing or monitoring input

cad.pattern: At each selected control or monitoring temperature point
cad.placement: On pipe surface, in sensor pocket or within equipment
cad.start: Thermal contact with water or pipe
cad.opening: Probe, clip and cable can be serviced
cad.load: Light device carried by pocket, pipe clip or equipment

notes: The measured system role—flow, return, tank or mixed circuit—is mandatory metadata.

objects.name: hydronic outdoor-temperature sensor
objects.definition: A weather-resistant external air-temperature sensor used by a hydronic controller to adjust heating-water temperature or output with outdoor conditions.

cad.pattern: One sensor per weather-compensated controller
cad.placement: Representative external wall position according to selected product instructions
cad.opening: Sensor vents remain exposed and cable penetration is sealed
cad.load: Light fixture fixed to external wall

notes: Avoid hard-coding one compass orientation; manufacturer instructions and local solar exposure determine placement.
